checks.label: dead-symbol-no-consumer-or-definition
checks.heading: ### 14. Added symbol, include, parameter, branch or header needs a consumer at HEAD
checks.skill_md:
Trigger: diff adds a name, an `#include`, a parameter, an `if` an enclosing guard decides, a second `TRACE_EVENT_END` (span end), or a header nothing includes.

Procedure:
1. `git grep -n -w NAME HEAD -- h src t bin ingest`, minus its declaration; zero is an item.
2. Zero callers: a comment promising an action ("clear", "called between") leads to the lifecycle code.
3. Include X in F: grep F for X's names at HEAD and BASE.

Question: Which line at HEAD uses this, or what is it for?

Do not fire on: test-only helpers (ask for a label, 3866590750); author-declared kept-for-later code; dead code outside the diff ("fwiw", 3866653656); an include used only under an off debug switch (debug-switch owns it); lift-PR minor items (one "fwiw" line).

Finding shape: "I don't see where `<name>` is used? (<file:line>) Just for completion/future enhancement?"

Severity and precedent: never "nit"; minor when the leftover compiles to nothing; normal when a consumer or definition is missing (3029165954). n = 21 comments over 12 PRs, 2026-01-26-2026-08-26.
checks.question_line: 14. Dead symbol: which line at HEAD, other than its own declaration, reads, calls, includes or compiles this, and if none does, what is it in the PR for?
checks.procedure_md:
## Check 14: added symbol, include, parameter, branch or header needs a consumer

Setup: `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.ref))`; on a merged PR (returns HEAD) use `--jq .base.sha`.

1. Constants: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -oE '^\+\s*(inline\s+)?(static\s+)?constexpr\s+[A-Za-z_0-9:]+\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*' | awk '{print $NF}' | sort -u`
2. Functions: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -E '^\+(inline |static )?[A-Za-z_:<>]+ [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' | grep -vE ';\s*$' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\(' | tr -d '(' | sort -u`; drop names `git -C WT grep -w "$n" BASE -- h src t bin` finds; aliases: `grep -E '^\+\s*(using [A-Za-z_]+ =|extern )'` on the diff over h src t.
3. Consumers: `git -C WT grep -n -w "$n" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v -E "constexpr [A-Za-z_0-9:]+ $n *=" | wc -l` (`-w`, never `NAME\s*\(`).
4. Promise: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n "$((L-10)),${L}p" | grep -n -i -E 'called (between|after|before|on|when)|reset|clear|release'`
5. Definition: `git -C WT grep -n -E "^[A-Za-z].* $n\(" HEAD -- src h`
6. Includes: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD | grep -E '^\+\+\+ |^\+#include'`; per X in F: `git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep -n -w -E 'NAME1|NAME2' | grep -v '#include'`, same on `BASE:F`; `git -C WT log --format='%h %s' --no-merges BASE..HEAD -- F`; `git -C WT show HEAD:F | grep '^#include' | sort | uniq -d`
7. Parameters: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^@@ -[0-9]+,0 \+[0-9]+ @@ .*[A-Za-z_]+\(' -A1`; then `git -C WT grep -n 'FUNC(' HEAD -- h src t`
8. Branches: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+\s*if \('`; `git -C WT diff -U3 BASE HEAD | grep -n -A3 -E 'ASSERT\(false|std::unreachable|abort\('`; `grep -n 'TRACE_EVENT_END("SPAN")'` on `HEAD:FILE`
9. Headers: `for f in $(git -C WT diff --name-only BASE HEAD -- 'h/*.hpp'); do git -C WT grep -l -E "#include .*$(basename $f)" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v "^HEAD:$f$" | wc -l; done`
10. Lift: `gh pr view N --json title,body | grep -i -E 'step [0-9]|phase [0-9]|lifts?\b|pulls? in'`

checks.label: typo-or-wording-in-added-text
checks.heading: ### 14. Spelling, wrong names and over-wide lines in added prose
checks.skill_md:
Trigger: added C++ comment or string literal (h/, src/, t/, doc/), or .md line outside a fence.

Procedure:
1. prose.py (references/check14/) on `git diff BASE HEAD`.
2. spell.py (pyspellchecker dictionary) against a `git grep` allow list (BASE words, HEAD identifiers, basenames); read uncorrected hits.
3. step5.py: comment token, whole-tree count 1, one-letter-edit code neighbour.
4. width.py: .md line over 1.25 times the widest unchanged hunk line; read for repeated words.

Question: does the line hold an unknown word, a name one letter from a symbol, or an over-wide Markdown line?

Do not fire on: context lines; commit subjects, PR body; resolving code tokens; lowercase sentence start; new .md files, tables, fences, URLs; grammar.

Finding shape: one ```suggestion block holding the corrected line (3307296300); over-wide line: formatter question (3778051701), repeat "same here" (3778058064).

Severity and precedent: nit, usually unstated (16 of 19 bare blocks), never blocking (3125494616 one minute before APPROVED 4156364038). n = 19 comments over 8 PRs (tron 2011, 2078, 2148, 2233, 2499, 2766, 2903, 3386), 2026-02-10 to 2026-08-13.

## Check 14: spelling, wrong names and over-wide lines in added prose

BASE: open PR `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.ref))`; merged PR `BASE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .base.sha)`. Scripts: references/check14/.

1. `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD > pr.diff; python3 -I prose.py WT HEAD pr.diff > prose.txt`
2. `{ git -C WT grep -ohE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{2,}' BASE -- h src t; for f in $(grep '^+++ b/' pr.diff | sed 's#^+++ b/##' | grep -E '^(h|src|t)/.*\.(hpp|cpp|h|c|inl)$'); do git -C WT show HEAD:$f | sed -E 's#//.*$##; s#"([^"\\]|\\.)*"##g' | grep -v -E '^\s*(\*|/\*)' | grep -oE '[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{2,}'; done; git -C WT ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD | sed 's#.*/##; s#\..*$##'; } | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr '_' '\n' | grep -E '^[a-z]{3,}$' | sort -u > lexicon.txt`
3. `uv run -q --with pyspellchecker python -I spell.py prose.txt lexicon.txt > spell.txt; grep -E '^(BAD|VOCAB)' spell.txt` (fallback `uvx codespell prose.txt`)
4. `for w in $(grep EXCUSED spell.txt | grep -v '(affix)\|(prefix)' | awk '{print $2}'); do s=${w%s}; c=$(git -C WT grep -n -i -E "$s" HEAD -- h src t | sed -E 's#//.*$##; s#"([^"\\]|\\.)*"##g' | grep -v -E '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:\s*(\*|/\*)' | grep -i -c -E "$s"); [ "$c" -eq 0 ] && echo "read: $w"; done`
5. `uv run -q --with pyspellchecker python -I step5.py WT HEAD prose.txt | grep '^FIND'`
6. `for f in $(git -C WT diff --name-only BASE HEAD -- '*.md'); do echo "== $f"; git -C WT show HEAD:$f | awk '/^```/{f=!f} !f && /^#/{print NR": "$0}'; done`

checks.label: magic-literal-or-constant-name
checks.heading: ### 13. A number in production code carries its role
checks.skill_md:
Trigger: in h/ or src/: a bare literal above 1 in a changed function; a literal in a removed name's slot; a stale message after a constant change; an underived sizing constant; a count constant as failure value; a suffixed constant in shared code beside a partner's named local.

Procedure:
1. Grep added lines, comments stripped, for literals above 1 the removed line lacked.
2. Grep the file, h/pos/config.hpp and includes for that value.
3. Pair removed names with added lines; `git log -m -S` finds merge artifacts.

Question: what does this number measure, and why did its name leave?

Do not fire on: 0, 1; unchanged lines unless the diff touches their replacing constant; `/ 2` still explained; t/; SIMD, diagnostics; accessor-computed values (duplicate-logic); clamp bounds (silent-fallback); suffixes in the author's kernel files; deferrals.

Finding shape: "`<expr>` (<file:line>) hard-codes <N>; <config:line> names it `<name>`. Use it? Nit."

Severity and precedent: nit (`non-blocking nit`, 6021333114); design question for sizing. n = 18 comments over 13 PRs, 2025-12-15 to 2026-10-06.

## Check 14: explanation at the declaration

1. Parameters: `grep -n -E '^\+[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_:<>*&]+ [A-Za-z_0-9]+ = [^,;()]+(,|\)[^;{]*\{)$' pr.diff`. Leading comment: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | head -n $((LINE-1)) | tac | awk '/^[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*|\/\*)/ {print; next} NF {exit}' | tac | grep -c NAME` (0 = candidate). Hedge words: hint|tmp|temp|opt|maybe|hack. Callers: `git -C WT grep -n -A6 'FUNCTION(' HEAD -- h src t`; drop if no hedge word and a caller omits it.
2. Env vars: `grep -n -E '^\+.*getenv\("([A-Z0-9_]+)"' pr.diff`; drop VAR read on a `-` line or by `git -C WT grep -c 'getenv("VAR")' BASE -- h src t bin` elsewhere; then `git -C WT grep -n -w VAR HEAD -- README*.md doc h src t bin | grep -v 'getenv("VAR")'` (0 = candidate).
3. Routines, per f in prfiles.txt: `git -C WT show HEAD:$f | awk -v F=$f '/^(static |inline |template)?[A-Za-z_:<>*&, ]+ [A-Za-z_0-9:]+\(.*\)[^;]*\{$/ && $0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*:/ && prev !~ /^[[:space:]]*(\/\/|\*|\*\/|\/\*)/ {print F":"NR": "$0} {if ($0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*$/ && $0 !~ /^[[:space:]]*(TRON\(|template[[:space:]]*<|\[\[|#)/) prev=$0}'`; keep `+` definitions absent at BASE (`git -C WT show BASE:FILE | grep -c 'NAME('` = 0). Length: `awk -v L=LINE 'NR>=L {n++; d+=gsub(/\{/,"{"); d-=gsub(/\}/,"}"); if (d>0) seen=1; if (seen && d==0) {print n; exit}}'` (keep >= 20). One nit per PR.
4. Test-only helpers: `awk '/^diff --git/{f=$3} /^@@/ && f ~ /^a\/h\// {print f": "$0}' pr.diff | sed 's/@@.*@@//' | sort -u`; per NAME `git -C WT grep -n -E "\bNAME\(" HEAD -- h src t bin ingest | grep -v -E "HEADER:(DEFLINE|DOCLINE)"` (all t/ = test-only). Trigger: an added line frees or submits a DMA buffer (DMA: hardware copier), reserves a literal beside a held reference, or hands SIMD an unaligned array.

Procedure:
1. Grep added lines for free, submit, destructors; classify drop paths (wait, leak, free); count commit-push copies.
2. Grep literal reserves, held references, growth calls; trace each to the next read.
3. Grep consumer overload for aligned intrinsics, compare element alignment, grep t/; UBSan or `Insufficient data`.

Question: after the free, submit or reallocation, who reads it, and is it aligned for the consumer?

Do not fire on: never-freed buffers (PR 1722); PR 2906 machinery (Note reworded, 3350285744); unaligned consumers; no literal reserve (PR 4353); wait sets, readiness predicates (siblings); `alignas` literals (check 13).

Finding shape: "`<buffer>` freed at :<n>; `<reader>` reads it. Fix: <release unless completed | alignas(<CONST>) like <sibling>> and a real-consumer test."

Severity and precedent: "Nit" (3120788282); "Fix:" (3960506641); "Top robustness item" (attributed: assistant text pasted by Wade in 5498556672); n=6 comments over 3 PRs (2499, 2906, 4128), 2026-04-21-2026-09-08, attributed.
checks.question_line: 14. Buffer: after the line that frees, submits or reallocates it, who still reads it, and does its declared alignment reach the consumer's widest aligned store?
checks.procedure_md:
## Check 14: buffer lifetime and alignment follow the consumer

Setup: `BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$(gh pr view N --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName))`. Force-pushed head: `gh api "repos/positron-ai/tron/contents/<path>?ref=HEAD" -q .content | base64 -d`.

1. `grep -nE '^\+[^/]*(dma_allocate|dma_deallocate|release_buffer|free_staging|abandon\(|\.pop\(\)|\.reset\(\)|xfer_(n_)?blocks\(|xfer_gofs?\(|dma_tracker::push|~[a-z_]+\(\)\s*\{)' pr.diff`
2. `git -C WT grep -n -E 'clear\(\)|~dma_tracker|q\.pop\(\)|\.reset\(\)|std::optional<pending_xfer>' HEAD -- src/pos/dma_tracker.cpp h/pos/dma_tracker.hpp`; each path waits, leaks or frees.
3. `git -C WT grep -n -E 'reservation\.commit\(\)|guard\.commit\(\)|\.push\(pending_xfer' HEAD -- h src`
4. `grep -nE '^\+.*\.reserve\([0-9]+\)' pr.diff`; per container V: `grep -nE '^\+.*&\s*[a-z_]+\s*=\s*V(\.(back|front)\(\)|\[)|= *V\.data\(\)' pr.diff`; `grep -nE '^\+.*V\.(push_back|emplace_back|insert|resize|assign|pop_back)\(' pr.diff`
5. `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | sed -n '<ref line>,<last use>p' | grep -n -E 'V\.(push_back|emplace_back|insert|resize|assign|pop_back)\(|continue;|break;|return'`
6. `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -nE '^\+.*(std::array<(bf16|float|uint8_t|__m256i|__m512i), *[A-Za-z_0-9]+>|^\+\s*(bf16|float|uint8_t) [a-z_]+\[)' | grep -v alignas`
7. `git -C WT grep -n '<member> =' HEAD -- h src t`; `START=<signature line>; END=$(awk -v s=$START 'NR>s && /^}/ {print NR; exit}' <file>); sed -n "${START},${END}p" <file> | grep -n -E '_mm256_(store|load)_si256|_mm512_(store|load)_(si512|ps|epi)|_mm512_stream'`
8. `git -C WT grep -n -E '^(struct|class) <T>\b' HEAD -- h`; `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n alignas`; `git -C WT grep -n -E '<consumer>\(' HEAD -- t/`
9. `grep -o -m1 avx2 /proc/cpuinfo`; `g++ -O1 -mavx2 -fsanitize=alignment -fno-sanitize-recover=alignment repro.cpp` (`array + 8` of an `alignas(64)` array).

On PR 4128 at 97de6ee02c (BASE 130ad3a652): step 6 src/tron/gof.cpp:436 `v_scratch`, passed :445, consumer h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2096, `_mm256_store_si256` :2109; bf16.hpp:12-13 2 bytes; sibling alignas gof.cpp:371; t_phase1_integration.cpp:890 copies. Step 2: `~dma_tracker` :58-68 calls clear() :67, clear() waits :180; at 442ed0dd1a `~dma_tracker` :57-61 skips clear(), `~gof_dma_batch` gof.cpp:40-42 frees. Step 3: gof.cpp:488, :511. On PR 2499 at 54a6fd7d1c (BASE 9ef4586a57, hwattention_sync): step 4 h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1395 `stk.reserve(64)`, refs :1403, :1956; step 5: push :1850, `break` :1854, `continue` :1858, pop :1953, re-take :1956; finding = question.

quotes.quote: gof.cpp:436 introduces an ordinary stack array, then passes it through v_head_into_fn to page::get_v(). That gather uses _mm256_store_si256, requiring 32-byte alignment.

Fix: add alignas(HWCACHEBLOCK_ALIGN_BYTES), matching the batch scratch, and exercise the real gather through singleton population. Current optimized Clang can mask the violation by fusing instructions
why 64? perhaps a comment explaining... I'm assuming a sufficiently deep-enough tree will still reallocate. How deep do we get in your tests?
if you do `push_back` enough times to exceed 64 and it has to reallocate, it will invalidate any **references** you are currently holding. Whereas, a std::deque won't...

## How Wade reviews and words a finding

Words used here: PR = pull request. Text = one Wade comment or review body with words (269 on 115 PRs he did not author). Id = GitHub comment or review id. Row = classified item (239 rows).

### Two registers by date

Register A, 2025-09 to 2026-08 (230 of 269 texts): short (29 words average, 222 texts), lowercase start (126 of 222), a question (105 of 222), a suggestion block for a one-line fix (41 of 43 blocks).

- 2719160746 (PR 1920): "wrap in `#ifdef WRITEBACK_HEXDUMPS`?"
- 2771713070 (PR 1997): "don't need this bf16.hpp include now right?"

Register B, 2026-09 onward (39 of 269): long (98 words average), file:line (10 of 39), a code fact, the consequence after "So", an ask with two repairs.

- 4188336256 (PR 4557): "it sits after the `available()` early return (line 197), so it silently skips on hosts without AMX. ... Move it above the early return, or into t_llama_unit."
- 5420005787 (PR 4557 review): "**Commits**: 20, three of them rewording one Note. Please squash."

Pick by the finding, not the date. Never write "LGTM" or a directive "must" (0 of 269 each).

### Verdict calibration

- 334 reviews: 100 APPROVED, 234 COMMENTED, 0 CHANGES_REQUESTED.
- Verdict by top-level comment count (115 PRs): 0 comments, 57 of 58 APPROVED; 1 to 2, 21 of 31; 3 to 5, 9 of 12; 6 or more, 11 of 14.
- Four must-change signals: "before merge" (3124878965), "needs" (3002050036), "Please <verb>" (5420005787), withheld approval (16 of 67 PRs with Wade text, PR 2089 among them).
- 48 silent PRs (no Wade words): median 2 files and 39 changed lines, versus 7 files and 410 lines for the 65 PRs with inline or review-body text. Small, mechanical or doc-only changes pass silently at any commit count.

### Pasted assistant text

Nine of 269 texts disclose a paste from Claude, "CC" or GPT: 3002297607, 4131374395, 3342904643, 4674512577, 3437517809, 4800935083, 5498556672, 5544513215, 3970590653. Quote the frame sentence as Wade and the block as "assistant text pasted by Wade in <id>". His weight is the frame sentence, not the block. PR 4557: no disclosure in its 10 texts, markers match the disclosed-assisted PR 4128, so whether it was assisted is Insufficient data.

### What he rarely comments on

He does not comment on the C++ guide or kernel arithmetic line by line (0 of 269 texts each). He rarely comments on formatting or benchmark method: one text each, both a question or a wish, not an ask to fix. Add no findings on these items.

- Formatting: 1 of 269 (3778051701, a long Markdown line, as a question).
- Benchmark or measurement: 1 of 269 (4607543703, a wish for before/after metrics).
- Brace or indent: 1 of 269 (2976643305, a dead loop scope).
- Commit message wording: 0 of 269. Squash: 1 of 334 reviews.
- Expected values or tolerances in tests: 0 of 239 rows.
- CI workflow YAML: 1 of 243 inline comments (3580238651).
- Owner sign-off for a shared header: 1 of 115 PRs (4188336279).
- Running the test suite himself: 2 of 113 reviewed PRs.
- Security, licensing, Python style: 0 of 239 rows.

### Replying to Wade

- He concedes in writing after the author's fact: 2790148917 ("yeah, doh!"), 3102275102 ("Nevermind ;p"). An agent withdraws a nit the same way.
- He defers to the area owner (3277240111). Get that owner's written answer.
- He accepts "next iteration" (3405172585), so a declined preference gets one reason and a follow-up offer.
- About one in six substantive asks is declined and let stand (16 pushed back of 239 rows). Classify first: a must-change signal or a preference word ("nit", "trivial", "pedantic", "maybe").
- Answer a must-change with a fact at the reviewed head (file:line, commit id). Never write "LGTM", resolve a thread for him, or post without the author's approval.

# Wade's review style: full reference

Short version: Wade (GitHub login Wado-posi) writes in two registers, a short hand-written question through 2026-08 and a long file:line finding from 2026-09 onward, and he never uses CHANGES_REQUESTED (0 of 334 reviews). A must-change is carried by the words "before merge", "needs", "Please <verb>" or by withheld approval. Nine of his 269 texts are disclosed pastes from an AI assistant and are quoted as attributed material, not as his words.

Words used here: PR = pull request. Corpus = the 115 PRs Wade reviewed and did not author (corpus.json plus pr/*.md under exec/wade-20261006/corpus/). Text = one Wade inline comment, review body with words, or conversation comment (269 texts: 243 inline, 11 conversation, 15 review bodies). Id = the GitHub comment or review id. Counts come from style-stats.json, merged-taxonomy.json and codex-factcheck.md; "recount" marks a count made for this document. ## How Wade words a finding

Words used here: PR = pull request. Text = one Wade comment, review body or conversation comment in the corpus (269 texts on 115 PRs he did not author: 243 inline, 11 conversation, 15 review bodies with words). Top-level text = a text that is not a reply (232 of 269). Id = the GitHub comment or review id. Counts come from style-stats.json (computed by style_stats.py over corpus.json) unless marked "recount".

Two registers exist, split by date. Match the register to the date and the length of the finding.

### Register A: hand-written, 2025-09 to 2026-08 (230 of 269 texts)

- Short: average 29 words per text (2026-01 to 2026-08, 222 texts; recount). Median top-level text is 132 characters and 2 sentences (232 top-level texts). The 90th percentile is 548 characters.

- Severity words, 232 top-level texts: "nit" 13, "trivial" 3, "minor" 3, "follow-up" 3, "non-blocking" 1. "LGTM" 0. "squash" 1.
- Humor markers ("lol", ";p", ":)") in 18 of 232 top-level texts. Ellipses "..." in 96 of 269 texts (recount).
- File:line citations: 1 of 222 texts in 2026-01 to 2026-08 (recount with a narrow pattern; codex-factcheck.md claim 7 counts 3 of 222 with a wider pattern).

Verbatim examples, register A:

- 4125033686 (PR 4596, 2026-09-28), opening and ask: "Design question on row sizing. "Was keying by attention worker index (instead of pool worker index) deliberate? Keying by pool worker index would make per-worker rows stable per thread/core, and the fold could skip workers with no bits set in the forward."
- 5420005787 (PR 4557 review, 2026-10-05): "**Commits**: 20, three of them rewording one Note. Please squash."

### Rules for an agent writing in his name

- Pick the register by the finding, not by the date alone. A one-line fix gets a suggestion block and a short question (register A). A finding that needs a fact, a consequence and two repairs gets register B with file:line.
- Backticked identifiers, with the location in the same clause.
- Every drop request names what to keep. Every text-versus-code mismatch offers both repairs.
- A design concern is a question with two alternatives ("deliberate, or key by ..."), not an order.
- Never write "LGTM" (0 of 269 texts). Never write "must" as a directive (0 of 269; codex-factcheck.md claim 6).

### How to treat a paste

- The pasted block is the assistant's claim. Wade's own words are the frame sentence around it. Quote the frame as Wade; quote the block as "assistant text pasted by Wade in <id>".
- Wade's weight on a pasted item is the frame sentence, not the block. "I think CC is onto something" (4131374395), "I do think there's some merit to a few of them" (4800935083) and "it agrees" (3970590653) are endorsements. "could be a follow-up if you prefer" (4800935083) and "Maybe it won't materialize" (4674512577) are not must-changes.
- A paste can carry words Wade never uses himself. "Blocking" in 5544513215 is in the pasted block; Wade's own texts never use "blocking" except as "non-blocking" (6021333114). "must" as a directive appears only inside pasted text.
- A pasted list is answered item by item, with a fact per item, and the reply is addressed to Wade.
- A paste is not independent verification. When a pasted item cites a line, re-check the line at the reviewed head before conceding it.

### What an agent drafting a reply does

1. Classify the ask by its wording. "before merge", "needs", "Please <verb>" or withheld approval (see Verdict calibration) is a must-change. "nit", "trivial", "minor", "pedantic", "next iteration", "no action needed", "maybe" is a preference.
2. For a must-change, answer with a fact at the reviewed head: what changed, the file:line, and the commit id. If the ask names two repairs, say which one was taken and why.
3. For a correct ask, concede the substance in one sentence and state the change. Do not restate his finding back to him.
4. For an ask that is wrong in a detail, correct the detail with the line that decides it (he conceded on 2790148917 and 3102275102; for 2790148917 the author's intervening reply was not read, so the deciding line is inferred, codex-factcheck.md claim 8 item 11). Keep the substance if it holds. Never post a replacement sentence that the checks have not verified (SKILL.md setup item 5).
5. For a preference that the author declines, give the reason in one sentence and offer a follow-up or "next iteration". He accepts both (3405172585, 2948027543). Do not argue style.
6. For a pasted assistant list, reply item by item with a fact each, addressed to Wade. Weight each item by his frame sentence ("merit", "could be a follow-up", "it agrees"), not by the block's own severity words.
7. Match his register. A one-line question gets a one-line answer. A register B finding gets a fact, the consequence and the chosen repair, with file:line.
8. When he defers to a named owner, get that owner's written answer and cite it in the reply. Do not answer on the owner's behalf.
9. Never write "LGTM", never mark the thread resolved on his behalf, and never post a reply the author has not approved. A review request authorizes analysis, not comment posting.
